newsitem.title: UK: UK output prices unchanged in November.
newsitem.headline: UK output prices unchanged in November.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following provisional data on UK input and output prices in November.(Prev data in brackets)
INPUT PRICES EX F, D, T, P (unadj)
INPUT PRICES EX F, D, T, P (adj)
INPUT COMPONENTS PCT CHANGE NOV M/M NOV Y/Y

Consensus of economists forecasts was for input prices to fall a seasonally adjusted 0.8 percent in November and fall 2.6 percent year-on-year. Output prices are forecast up 0.1 percent and 2.2 percent higher year-on-year.
* The ONS said the year-on-year change in core output prices showed the lowest rate of increase since September 1967.
The ONS said the budget measures would provisionally push up the output price index by 0.7 percent in December. But that represents about the same effect as the 1996 budget.
# The seasonally adjusted fall in input prices of 3.2 percent, was the largest fall since April 1985.
The ONS said the fall in input prices saw widespread falls in prices of commodities, reflecting sterling's appreciation.
That was partly offset by a seasonal rise in the costs of electricity.
The 5.5 percent year-on-year fall in input prices was the largest since December 1986.
